summary: An excerpt from a novel's interview scene in which Carly Grove, a single woman who adopted a baby named Kevin through Children of Light, describes paying about sixty thousand dollars for the adoption, with the baby arriving within three months and little knowledge of his origin. The narrator, a filmmaker shooting a documentary, sees the interview as powerful footage, then privately asks Carly whether she knows other single women who adopted through the agency, saying she may want to check them out herself. Carly, uneasy, begins to mention another woman who adopted from the agency.
one_line: A filmmaker interviews Carly Grove about her costly, rushed adoption through Children of Light and quietly asks for other referrals.
key_facts: Carly Grove says the money the adoption required was 'stagger­ing', totaling sixty thousand dollars.
Carly says it took her almost half a year to gather the money, with several credit lines maxed out.
Carly says she had Kevin in less than three months after paying the money.
Carly says she does not know where Kevin came from, though she believes he was probably from out of the country because of blank INS forms she signed.
Carly says 'With a deal this good, you don't press for details, right?'
The adoption miracle in the interview is attributed to a doctor named Goddard.
The narrator wants to get the film to the lab and see the rushes, and has a doctor's appointment that afternoon.
The time is pushing two o'clock when the narrator suggests ending the interview.
The narrator plans a meeting with David to update him on the project.
Roger Drexel uses a Panaflex camera and hides his thoughts in his scraggly beard.
Marcy is feeding Kevin Gerber applesauce in the kitchen.
The narrator asks Carly whether she knows other single women who adopted through Children of Light.
The narrator tells Carly she may want to check out other adoptive women for herself.
Carly mentions that her lawyer first told her about Children of Light and gave her the name of another adoptive woman.
Carly starts twisting her hair when she becomes worried about the narrator's questions.
